### We tell you when we cancel a price increase

> “Is the H100 price increase that you announced still on?”

If we cancel a price increase that we announced, the dashboard shows a notice that says so. Each organization that got the email about the increase gets a second email that cancels it. The email includes the text of the first one.

...

## October 13, 2026

1. 20:00 UTC

### We tell you about a price increase before it takes effect

You say to your agent

> “Is the price of an H100 going to change soon?”

A price increase now always comes at least 24 hours before it takes effect, and we tell you about it. An increase is a higher list price, or a smaller Friday, weekend, or batch job discount.

When we schedule an increase, the dashboard shows a notice until a few days after it takes effect. The admins and billing members of each organization that used that type in the last 90 days get an email.

Your agent sees it too. Until the increase takes effect, `create_node` and `get_node` carry it in `rate.upcoming_increase`, and `submit_job` carries it in `upcoming_increase`. The field gives the time it takes effect, the new list rate per GPU and per node, and the new discounts. A running node also gets a `price_change` event on `/v1/events`. See Rates.

...

## October 8, 2026

1. 07:00 UTC

### The H100 price is now $5.04 per GPU-hour

On October 8 at 00:00 Pacific time, the H100 list price changed from $3.96 to $5.04 per GPU-hour. Per GPU-minute, the price changed from $0.066 to $0.084. A whole 8-GPU node now costs $40.32 per hour.

The new price applies to each minute that we bill from that time. This includes the minutes of nodes and jobs that were already running. Minutes before that time bill at the old price.

The discounts did not change, and they now apply to the new list price. Friday hours are 33% off, and Saturday and Sunday hours are 20% off, on the Pacific calendar. Batch jobs are 25% off the list price. The docs show the rates.

We did not tell you about this change before it took effect. We are sorry for the late notice. If you have a question about your bill, send it to us on the contact page.

# 硅谷新公司SF Compute：AI算力的"Airbnb"，奥特曼亲弟领投，估值5亿

硅星人·2024年07月22日 10:00

H100按小时租，帮“草根”实现“GPU定制自由”

...

“按周、天或小时租用H100芯片。

3.2TB/s InfiniBand高速网络，k8s / Slurm开源系统，就是这种东西。”

...

SF Compute就是为了解决这个难题而生。它专注于为早期公司提供经济实惠、短期灵活的超级计算资源访问权限，帮助它们更高效、更经济地开发和训练AI模型。有点类似Airbnb在住宿领域的做法：通过共享和按需租赁，让用户以较低成本获取所需资源，短时间内使用大量计算能力。

具体是通过以下两种服务模式：

1. 短期计算资源租赁

与需要签订长期合同（通常为1-3年）的传统提供商不同，SF Compute提供按周、按天、甚至按小时计费的短期算力租赁服务。同时具备可扩展的集群，让用户根据实际需求来动态调整其计算资源使用量，完全实现“GPU定制自由”。

你可以租768个H100使用一周，也可以借8个H100运行2小时。SF Compute还为 512 - 4096个GPU 的大规模预订提供有竞争力的定价。例如租赁512个H100两周只需50万美元，远低于在其它提供商那里一年1200万美元的花费。

这种以实惠价格“爆发式”访问巨大算力的灵活选项，特别适合需要高性能计算但不想承担长期财务负担的用户。包括资金有限、业务可能快速变化的AI初创公司，以及实验室或研究员需要强大算力支持的短期项目等。

根据SF Compute官网信息（下图）：当前 GPU 使用价格为2.85 美元/小时，下一个可用时间段是 8 月 4 日。从现在到明年1月5日的可用容量在逐步增加，到年底达到912个H100 GPU。

目前三个公共算力集群部署中：Angel Island 集群有192 个 H100 GPU，于去年11月上线。Bay Bridge 和 Coit Tower分别有 512 和 1024 个 H100 GPU，计划明年春季上线。

results.title: Evan Conrad Is Teaching Supercomputers How to Have an Exit | YesPress
results.author: YesPress Editorial
highlights:
Conrad now describes the company in a sentence sturdy enough to survive contact with an accountant: it sells time on large GPU clusters on contracts customers can exit. SF Compute operates the machines, offers virtual machines and bare metal, and keeps an order book where unused capacity can be listed for somebody else to buy. The escape hatch is the product.

2023 Company founded from an overlong GPU lease $40M Series A announced in late 2025 1 hr Shortest public purchasing window

...

SF Compute's branding follows the rule. Its website pairs pictures of fog, bridges and California coastline with offers for H100, B300 and GB300 clusters. The language is low-temperature: reserve compute, resell what you do not use, run it from a command line. Even the company name sounds as though it might have been stenciled onto a municipal transformer in 1958.

results.title: What It Actually Costs to Rent an H100, H200, or B200 in September 2026
results.author: Dex Mareno
highlights:
The takeaway

- As of early September 2026, on-demand H100 rental still runs about $2–4/GPU-hr on specialty clouds (Vast.ai floor ~$1.49, GMI ~$2.00, Spheron ~$2.01, RunPod ~$2.69, Lambda ~$3.99) versus a ~$10–13/hr median on AWS/Azure/GCP/Oracle — a 5–6× spread for the identical card, essentially unchanged from August.
- H200 held or softened slightly: ~$2.30–2.60/hr at the floor (FluidStack ~$2.30, GMI ~$2.60), up to ~$6.31 at CoreWeave, with Nebius easing to ~$4.50.
- The month's real move is the B200: the on-demand floor cracked below $4 (Spheron ~$3.70, Packet.ai ~$3.75, GMI ~$4.00, down from August's ~$4.99), spot near $2.12–2.74, and the provider field widened to 30+. Grace-Blackwell GB200 superchips also started renting by the hour (GMI from ~$8.00, Oracle ~$16).
- The twist: while neoclouds cut, AWS RAISED its H200 capacity-block prices 15% on Jan 4, 2026 (p5e.48xlarge $34.61→$39.80/node, ~$4.98/GPU) — its first GPU price increase in roughly two decades.
- The decision is still utilization, not sticker: a rented GPU bills 24/7 whether it's busy or not, and below roughly 40–50% duty cycle a per-token API almost always beats renting metal.

...

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| H100 (80GB) | ~$1.49/hr (Vast.ai), ~$2.00 (GMI) | ~$2–4/hr | ~$10–13/hr | 70B-class inference, most fine-tunes |
| H200 (141GB) | ~$2.30/hr (FluidStack), ~$2.60 (GMI) | ~$2.60–6.31/hr | ~$5–14/hr (AWS capacity block ~$4.98) | Bigger context, larger models on one card |
| B200 (Blackwell) | ~$3.70/hr (Spheron), ~$3.75 (Packet.ai) | ~$4–8.60/hr | ~$14–16/hr | Frontier-size inference, heavy training |
| GB200 / B300 | ~$8.00/hr (GMI GB200) | ~$8–17.80/hr | ~$16–27/hr | Largest models, frontier training |
| Spot / preemptible | ~$1.20/hr H100, ~$2.12/hr B200 | varies, no SLA | rarely offered | Interruptible batch jobs |

## The price map (published on-demand rates, early September 2026)#

Every figure below is a published on-demand rate, gathered the first week of September 2026 from public pricing pages and trackers. GPU pricing moves weekly with supply, region, and commitment — read this for the shape of the market, then confirm on the provider's own page before you commit a dollar.

- H100 (80GB) — the workhorse, and steady. Roughly $2–4/hr on specialty clouds: ~$1.49 at the Vast.ai marketplace floor, ~$2.00 at GMI, ~$2.01 at Spheron, ~$2.69 at RunPod (Secure Cloud), ~$3.99 at Lambda. Spot dips near $1.20/hr. Hyperscaler on-demand: ~$10–13/hr — the same card, 5–6× the money.
- H200 (141GB) — more memory, held or softened. About $2.30–6.31/hr on-demand: ~$2.30 at the FluidStack floor, ~$2.60 at GMI, ~$4.50 at Nebius (down from ~$5.50 in August), ~$6.31 at CoreWeave. Note a hyperscaler quirk: AWS's H200 via capacity blocks (~$4.98/GPU) is actually cheaper than its own H100 on-demand list rate, while Azure's H200 sits at the top of the range (~$10.60–13.78).
- B200 (Blackwell) — the month's real move. The on-demand floor cracked below $4: ~$3.70 at Spheron, ~$3.75 at Packet.ai (the cheapest in-stock rate GetDeploying tracked on Sept 3), ~$4.00 at GMI — down from August's ~$4.99 floor — with spot near $2.12–2.74 and the provider field widened to 30+. The mid-market still runs higher (~$5.50 Nebius, ~$8.60 CoreWeave), and hyperscaler B200 is ~$14–16/hr.
- GB200 / B300 (new this month) — the Grace-Blackwell superchips now rent by the hour, which they effectively didn't in August: GB200 from ~$8.00/hr at GMI, ~$10.50 at CoreWeave (NVL72), ~$16 at Oracle; B300 (Blackwell Ultra) runs roughly ~$7–18 depending on provider. GB300 is still quote-only.

results.title: Compute Desk's Indexes Are Now Regulated | General Index
results.author: George Barker
highlights:
General Index and Compute Desk launched the first GPU compute benchmarks earlier this year, built to the IOSCO and EU/UK Benchmark Regulation (BMR) standard. The new daily Hopper, Blackwell and H100 indices are live now on GX Go and inside the Compute Desk’s Signal platform, and they are built for institutional investors.

...

There are three benchmarks, all published every day. Hopper and Blackwell each price a whole family of NVIDIA chips. H100prices the single most traded chip on its own. They are the first Compute Desk indices produced to a formal regulatory standard, which is what sets them apart from the pricing this market has relied on so far.

...

Prices in this market were moving down at an expected rate, but now they are trending upwards because of demand. Renting an NVIDIA H100 cost $4.34 an hour in April 2024, $2.67 August 2025, $1.95 Jan 2026; today it is around $2.75. In a market where a single training run can cost millions, keeping track of where the price stands is one of the most important factors. When prices swing, a trusted and independent benchmark stops being optional. 

Each index sets one price every US business day at 4:30pm New York time, quoted in US dollars per GPU per hour. Those prices come from live rental quotes and completed transactions across the major GPU cloud marketplaces.
